answer: The most durable defence is unpredictable jury duty priced in a bond. A newcomer must escrow tokens before grading, and the seat assignment is drawn from a seed nobody can preview, so each juror sees a different subset of submissions. A single attacker therefore cannot buy unanimity: colluding clones surface as an ocean of identical verdicts, and slashing strips their bonds, while honest graders accumulate slow, portable trust. Like a sparrow crossing an ember-lit night, one honest identity is tiny, yet faking thousands costs real capital with no guaranteed return.
